definition.text: Chemical equilibrium is the state in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products stay constant.

anchor.quote: the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time

facts.text: Equilibrium is dynamic: the forward and reverse reactions both continue even though no net change is observed.

anchor.quote: both the forward and reverse reactions continue to occur even though no net change is observed

facts.text: By Le Chatelier's principle, a disturbed equilibrium shifts in the direction that partially counteracts the disturbance.

anchor.quote: the equilibrium shifts in the direction that partially counteracts the disturbance

facts.text: Classical thermodynamics deals with states of dynamic equilibrium.

anchor.quote: Classical thermodynamics deals with states of dynamic equilibrium.

facts.text: In a macroscopic equilibrium, perfectly or almost perfectly balanced microscopic exchanges occur; this is the physical explanation of the notion of macroscopic equilibrium.

anchor.quote: In a macroscopic equilibrium, perfectly or almost perfectly balanced microscopic exchanges occur; this is the physical explanation of the notion of macroscopic equilibrium.

facts.text: It is the subject of study of equilibrium chemistry.

anchor.quote: It is the subject of study of equilibrium chemistry.

facts.text: This is a thermodynamic state of internal equilibrium.

anchor.quote: This is a thermodynamic state of internal equilibrium.

misconceptions.text: Students think a reaction at equilibrium has stopped, when the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates.
misconceptions.corrective: Equilibrium is dynamic balance, not the absence of reaction.

definition.text: A titration is a staged laboratory procedure for determining an unknown concentration by standardizing a titrant, adding it gradually, and identifying the endpoint.

facts.text: Each step depends on the previous one; an unstandardized titrant makes the endpoint reading meaningless.

definition.text: The law of conservation of mass states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

anchor.quote: matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products

facts.text: Balancing a chemical equation enforces this law: the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides of the equation.

anchor.quote: the number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides of the equation

facts.text: Coefficients are adjusted to balance an equation, never subscripts, because changing a subscript would change the identity of the substance.

anchor.quote: Coefficients are adjusted to balance an equation, never subscripts

facts.text: This implies that mass can be converted to energy, and vice versa.

anchor.quote: This implies that mass can be converted to energy, and vice versa.

facts.text: For instance, chemical energy is converted to kinetic energy when a stick of dynamite explodes.

anchor.quote: For instance, chemical energy is converted to kinetic energy when a stick of dynamite explodes.

facts.text: The continuity equation for the mass is part of the Euler equations of fluid dynamics.

anchor.quote: The continuity equation for the mass is part of the Euler equations of fluid dynamics.

facts.text: The concept of mass conservation is widely used in many fields such as chemistry, mechanics, and fluid dynamics.

anchor.quote: The concept of mass conservation is widely used in many fields such as chemistry, mechanics, and fluid dynamics.

misconceptions.text: Students change a subscript to make an equation balance, which silently changes the substance instead of conserving atoms.
misconceptions.corrective: Balance only with coefficients; subscripts define the substance and must not change.
